samples.summary: adjudicationNote's fallback label declares "the overturn lacked grounded evidence" for any adjudication object with no `verdict` — which is exactly the shape every carried-forward finding has
samples.evidence: severity.mjs:121-126 builds the label as `upheld` / `unresolved` / `errored`, else `**upheld** (the overturn lacked grounded evidence)`. The else branch is reached whenever `a.verdict` is absent, and that is the normal carry-forward shape: agent-review-panel.yml:909 persists only `adjudication: Number.isInteger(f.adjudication?.upheld) ? { upheld: f.adjudication.upheld } : undefined` — the verdict string and reason are deliberately dropped — and prior-findings.mjs:106 re-hydrates the finding with `{...f, lens}`, preserving `{upheld:N}` verbatim. Those prior findings flow through annotateFindings (review-panel.mjs:2634) → keepUnrefuted → mergedAfter → writeVerdict (review-panel.mjs:3082) → renderSummaryMd, and adjudicateRebuttals only rewrites `adjudication` for findings matched to a rebuttal posted THIS round (review-panel.mjs:2117-2143). So a finding disputed once and upheld in round 1, not re-disputed in round 2, renders in round 2's check body as "dispute adjudicated: **upheld** (the overturn lacked grounded evidence)" — a specific, false claim about an adjudication that did not happen this round and, when it did happen, reached a different verdict. The same path also erases a previous round's `skipped-by-author` (it loses the verdict, so it is mislabelled as an ungrounded overturn instead of being listed by authorSkipsSection at severity.mjs:164).

samples.summary: locatorOf can print a locator the lens never claimed: findingLocation returns the evidence citation's own file when the finding has no `file`
samples.evidence: locatorOf (severity.mjs:85-89) delegates to findingLocation, which at novelty.mjs:156-158 returns `{file: cited.file, line: cited.line}` when the finding carries no `file` — "No file on the finding → the citation is all we have, so take it whole." That rule is safe for a git probe (a wrong location only yields `unknown`), but here it is rendered as the row's authoritative locator. A finding whose file the lens left blank but whose evidence mentions any `x.ext:N` token (CITATION at citation.mjs:22 matches anywhere in the string, including a contrasting file) now renders `- \`other.mjs:7\` — summary` where it previously rendered `- summary`. harvest.mjs:443-451 then parses that row and records `file: "other.mjs"` into the eval corpus, where it can suppress a CodeRabbit candidate on a file the finding was never about.

samples.summary: The new `file:line` locator prints a stale offset for carried-forward findings, the exact reading the panel refuses to trust elsewhere
samples.evidence: The carry-forward whitelist (agent-review-panel.yml:909) drops `line` but keeps `evidence` (trimmed to 2000 chars), so for a prior-round finding locatorOf falls back to the first same-file citation inside that old evidence and renders `file:LINE`. review-panel.mjs:2627-2632 states the reason this is unsafe: "Their `line` was recorded against a previous round's HEAD, and the fixer has rewritten the tree since; that offset now points at whatever happens to sit there" — which is why carried-forward findings are deliberately not novelty-probed. The renderer now asserts that same untrusted offset to the human (and, via harvest's `evidence: at <locator>`, to extractAnchor) with no marker that it is from an earlier tree.

samples.summary: renderLedger adds an unbounded table to the summary comment, eating the headroom SUMMARY_DATA_BUDGET reserves under GitHub's 65 536-char cap
samples.evidence: metrics.mjs:57-59 documents SUMMARY_DATA_BUDGET = 55000 as "Keep summary body + data block under GitHub's 65 536-char comment cap", i.e. ~10.5k is reserved for the rendered body. renderLedger emits one ~55-char row per record with no cap, and cmdSummarize (metrics.mjs:1140-1141) posts `${summary}\n${serializeSummaryData(embedList)}` where the data block is sized against the budget without knowing the body grew. On a long-running PR (many implement/ci-fix/review/review-fix sessions) the combined body can cross the cap, and postComment failure is caught into `bail("could not post summary…")` — the round's summary is lost rather than truncated. The embed loop's budget check is the only size guard and it does not account for the table.

samples.summary: A confirmed verdict with a missing/other `confidence` is reported as "confirmed, low confidence"
samples.evidence: `out.verification = verdict.confidence === "high" ? "confirmed-high" : "confirmed-low"` treats every non-"high" value — including `undefined` from a verdict object whose confidence field did not come back — as an affirmative low-confidence statement, which severity.mjs:101 renders as "_(verifier: confirmed, low confidence)_". An absent confidence is not a measured low confidence; the same file's own rule elsewhere (metrics.mjs `measured`, guard-verdict `n()`) is to render an unmeasured value as unknown rather than coercing it to the pessimistic end.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. severity.mjs:121-125 falls through to "**upheld** (the overturn lacked grounded evidence)" for any adjudication object lacking `verdict`, and that is precisely the carry-forward shape: agent-review-panel.yml:909 persists only `{ upheld: N }` (verdict/reason intentionally dropped, per the comment at :900-908) and prior-findings.mjs:106 re-hydrates it as `{...f, lens}`. Consequently round 2 renders a specific false claim about an adjudication that did not occur this round, and a prior round's skipped-by-author is also mislabelled because authorSkipsSection (severity.mjs:164) keys on the verdict string that was dropped. Real, reachable, wrong-branch logic in the correctness lane; no refutation ground applies.
